subject: Pricing schedule markup: proration mechanics & fee coverage clarification
messages:
From: Mike Turner <mike.turner@bluepeaksys.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Anjali Desai <anjali@bluepeaksys.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify how proration and the fee coverage ladder interact

Kimberly,

Thanks for the call earlier. Before we kick off legal, a couple of clarifying items on the pricing schedule that will materially affect our procurement review:

- The "fee-protector" paragraph (section 2.3) reads like it guarantees a minimum monthly credit on scale-downs, but it's not explicit whether credits are applied pro rata within a billing month or only at month boundary. We need pro rata language if credits can be applied mid-month.
- The proposed ladder for volume credits (Exhibit B) includes a mid-tier smoothing clause; we want to confirm how the smoothing interacts with the cap/floor triggers — specifically whether a transient dip for 10 days should trigger a floor true-up.
- On rollback: your team suggested a 60-day review window. BluePeak's procurement requires a 90-day sustained threshold before a fee floor can be reduced.

Can you share a brief worked example (invoice-level) showing proration and the credit ladder mechanics across a scale-down scenario? That will speed our internal review.

Attached are the excerpted sections we're focused on.

Best,
Mike Turner
Sr. Procurement Manager
BluePeak Systems

Attachments: pricing_excerpt_BP.pdf (pdf stub)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Mike Turner <mike.turner@bluepeaksys.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Aug 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify how proration and the fee coverage ladder interact

Mike — thanks for laying this out clearly. I've looped in Marissa (sales), Aditya (legal), and Karthik (pricing/product) to propose a concise resolution. High level answers below, and we'll follow up with a worked example and a short markup showing adjusted language for the billing/proration paragraph.

1) Proration: we can and should make credits pro rata within the invoice period. Proposed text: "Credits earned during a billing period will be calculated pro rata based on days in the billing period during which the applicable usage tier applies, and applied on the subsequent invoice as an adjustment." We'll attach a sample invoice row to illustrate.

2) Transient dips: we agree that short transients (under 30 days) should not cause a floor true-up. Our suggested compromise: a 60-day rolling window before any permanent floor reduction is applied; pending that window, interim billing will reflect provisional credits that are subject to a 60-day true-up.

3) Review window: we understand your internal policy of 90 days. If BluePeak needs 90 days as a hard requirement, we can extend the rolling window to 90 days in the contract, but we will need to slightly adjust the smoothing clause in Exhibit B to maintain revenue protection. Aditya, can you propose redline language that increases the window to 90 days but clarifies provisional vs. permanent credits?

Next steps: Aditya will provide a short redline; Karthik will attach a 3-month invoice example. Marissa and I will coordinate to keep negotiations tight.

--
Kimberly Park
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify how proration and the fee coverage ladder interact

Kim / Team — quick commercial note from Sales: BluePeak is sensitive to any perceived clawback on credits. If we move to 90 days we should add a mitigating anchor for them: an annual true-up cap of 20% of total credits granted (so we don't have open-ended retrospective exposure). That keeps procurement comfortable while protecting Redwood economics.

Proposed sentence to add to Exhibit B: "Notwithstanding any provisional credits issued during the rolling window, the aggregate amount subject to retrospective adjustment in any 12‑month period shall not exceed 20% of credits granted in that period."

If legal is comfortable, I think that's an easy sell to BluePeak. Karthik, the invoice example should show a case where credits are provisionally applied and then a smaller retrospective adjustment at day 91.

— Marissa
Director, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify how proration and the fee coverage ladder interact — proposed legal language

Team / Mike — attached is a short redline (pricing_markup_v2.docx) with three changes:

A) Explicit proration language: "Credits arising from usage changes during a billing period shall be calculated on a pro rata basis relative to the number of days the applicable usage level was effective in that billing period and shall be reflected as an adjustment on the next invoice."

B) Rolling window extended: modified from 60 to 90 days per BluePeak request. Language includes: "A reduction in the applicable floor shall only be deemed permanent following a sustained decrease in average monthly usage below the floor threshold for a continuous period of ninety (90) days."

C) Annual true-up cap: I incorporated Marissa's 20% cap language and added a carveout for cases of fraud or material misreporting. Text: "Notwithstanding any provisional credits, retrospective adjustments pursuant to the rolling window shall not exceed twenty percent (20%) of credits granted in the immediately preceding twelve (12) month period, except where an investigation reasonably determines material misreporting or fraud."

Open questions for commercial: 1) Is the 20% cap acceptable as an absolute cap or should it be a softer guideline that triggers escalation? 2) Should the provisional credits be labelled "pending true-up" on the invoice to avoid disputes? I recommend 'pending true-up' label — it sets expectations.

Mike — please confirm if the 90-day window + 20% annual cap is acceptable and whether BluePeak requires the invoice label. If we get that confirmation, we can circulate the clean order form for signature.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Kim / Aditya / Team — thanks for the quick turnaround and the worked example — very helpful. BluePeak accepts the 90-day sustained window and the 20% annual true-up cap, provided two small clarifications:

1) Invoice labeling: yes, please mark provisional credits as "pending true-up" on the invoice. That will be surfaced to our finance reviewer and avoids confusion.
2) Administrative notice: if a retrospective adjustment will exceed $10,000 in a single invoice, please notify procurement and provide the calculation 30 days before the adjustment posts so we can prepare cashflow.

If you can confirm those two items in the final clean order form, we are good to proceed to signature.
